correctness.rationale: For all N>=3, nonempty S and strictly positive loss rates, diagonalize the uniform Peierls-cycle Hamiltonian with E_k=2J cos((2pi k+phi)/N). Away from 0/pi all eigenvalues are simple and plane waves cannot vanish on sinks. At ell*pi degenerate Fourier pairs k<- >-k-ell yield anchor-node vector; every remaining sink is nodal iff M=N/gcd(N,s-s0 for s in S) divides 2k+ell. Exactly G*gcd(2,M) solutions exist if gcd(2,M)|ell; remove fixed points of the involution (gcd(2,N) if it divides ell), divide by two. This proves the displayed dark dimension including all odd/even boundary cases. A=-iH-Gamma/2 has imaginary spectrum exactly on the reducing dark subspace and all complementary eigenvalues have negative real part, so limiting no-jump survival is the squared orthogonal dark projection, independent of positive loss strengths. For even N and a single site sink 0, at half flux the antipode belongs entirely to dark subspace and has survival one at every time, while at 0 flux it is dark-orthogonal. The modular-sink result and exact parity are the nontrivial steps; separate checks corroborate them, finite data are not a general proof.
